html:
Forbes Burnham was the Guyanese leader who took the country to independence in 1966 and ruled it until his death in 1985, as prime minister and then president.

A lawyer of African descent, he was a partner of Cheddi Jagan until he split from him in 1955 and later founded the People's National Congress, drawing support mostly from African Guyanese. With Western backing he came to power in 1964, and Guyana became independent on 26 May 1966.

In 1970 he declared a Cooperative Republic, nationalised bauxite and sugar, and banned many imports. Elections were rigged, critics such as Walter Rodney were attacked, and the economy shrank as many people emigrated. He also allowed the American cult leader Jim Jones to settle at Jonestown.
sum: Forbes Burnham was the Guyanese leader who took the country to independence in 1966 and ruled it until his death in 1985, as prime minister and then president.
